verdicts.note: Walking in the park, I met an old friend. Active simultaneous.
Feeling tired, she went to bed early. Reason.
Opening the door, he went out.
She sat on the sofa, reading a book. Simultaneous.
Hearing the news, she became very happy.
Not knowing what to say. Negation precedes participle.
Praised by everyone. Passive (past participle).
Seen from a distance. Passive.
Having finished the work. Perfect participle.
Not being tired. Negation precedes being.
It being sunny. Absolute construction with subject.
Being ill, he could not attend. Reason.
Generally speaking. Idiomatic participial phrase.
Having written the letter. Completion before main clause.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Walking down the street, I found the shop.
Not saying anything, he left the room.
verdicts.note: Token 'Not saying anything,' has trailing comma + capital N, so it must be fronted.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Having finished my homework, I watched TV.

verdicts.note: Token 'Smiling,' capitalized with comma forces it to the front; 'she' is lowercase.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Written in English, this book is easy to read.
verdicts.note: Passive participle fronted.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Seeing the dog, I ran away.
verdicts.note: When I saw -> Seeing.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Being tired, she took a rest.
verdicts.note: Because she was -> Being (not omitted as instructed).

verdicts.produced_sentence: When he saw the police officer, he ran away.
verdicts.note: Seeing -> When he saw.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Having eaten lunch, I went out.
verdicts.note: After I had eaten -> Having eaten (perfect participle).

verdicts.produced_sentence: Not knowing the answer, he stayed silent.
verdicts.note: As he did not know -> Not knowing.

verdicts.produced_sentence: Being written in easy English, the book sold well.
verdicts.note: Because it was -> Being written (passive, Being not omitted).
